intro_html: Taco night and spaghetti night stopped fighting for the calendar and merged: taco-seasoned beef, tomatoes, jalapenos, and two cheeses tangled through a pot of pasta. Each bowl brings 43 grams of protein and 603 calories for about $4.03 (at everyday cost). The kids will not ask questions; neither should you.
cost_closing_html: About $4.03 a bowl (at everyday cost) for cheesy taco pasta that beats the cost of one fast-casual burrito, and you get fourteen dinners instead of one.
shop_smart: The 93/7 ground beef carries most of the cost here, so grab the 4 lb pack for the better per-pound price and freeze the extra half pound.
Store-brand spaghetti runs under a dollar a box. It is the same durum wheat as the name brands; the only difference is the marketing budget you are not paying for.
Mix your own taco seasoning from chili powder, cumin, paprika, and garlic powder. The packets charge a serious markup per ounce for a tablespoon of spices.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the spaghetti in salted water until just shy of al dente, then drain, saving a cup of pasta water.
Meanwhile, brown the ground beef in your largest pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up, until no pink remains; ground beef should hit 160F. Drain excess fat.
Add the garlic and diced jalapenos and cook 2 to 3 minutes, then stir in the taco seasoning and tomato paste.
Pour in the diced tomatoes with their juice and simmer 8 to 10 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Fold in the spaghetti with a splash of the reserved pasta water, then stir in the Mexican cheese blend until it melts into the sauce.
Top with the mozzarella, cover on low heat 3 to 4 minutes until melted, then finish with the sliced olives and chopped cilantro.
portion_html: Weigh the loaded pot, subtract the empty-pot weight, and divide by 14. Tong even portions into 14 containers; twirl as needed. Each bowl checks in at 603 calories and 43 grams of protein.
upsell_html: Hearty dinners for about $4.03 a bowl (at everyday cost). This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

steps: Boil the spaghetti just shy of al dente and reserve a cup of pasta water.
Brown the beef to 160F, drain, then cook the garlic and jalapenos with taco seasoning and tomato paste.
Add the diced tomatoes and simmer 8 to 10 minutes.
Fold in the spaghetti and melt in the Mexican cheese blend.
Top with mozzarella, olives, and cilantro, then portion into 14 containers.
